findings.expected: Use a French banner (e.g. banner-fr.png) reading "Un financement adapté à vos projets — Taux concurrentiels. Modalités claires. Aucune surprise."
findings.description: The French landing page displays the English banner image with English text "Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises."
The footer copyright line is left in English on French pages.
The subtitle uses "tu" while the heading just above and the rest of the site use "vous".
"Appliquer pour" is an anglicism (calque of "apply for"); in Quebec French, use "Demander un prêt" or "Faire une demande de prêt".

findings.expected: Allow the button to grow (remove fixed width / overflow hidden) or use a shorter label such as "Soumettre la demande".
findings.description: The French submit button label is clipped: scrollWidth 290 vs clientWidth 210 with overflow hidden and nowrap.
"e-mail" is not the standard term in Canadian French; OQLF recommends "courriel".
The required-field error for the full name field is in English on the French form, while the other fields show the French message.

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande de 15 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: The confirmation shows a raw template token {montant} instead of the amount; the French string likely renamed the variable (the English uses the amount correctly).
"Balance" is an anglicism for an account balance; the correct banking term in French is "solde".
In French, zero takes the singular; the English plural rule was applied to the French string.
The section heading above the transactions table is left in English on the French dashboard.
Transaction dates on the French dashboard use the US MM/DD/YYYY format, which a French Canadian reader may misread as day/month (e.g. 09/12/2026 read as 9 December).
A bank "statement" is a "relevé" in French; "déclaration" means a declaration/filing, which is wrong in this context.
The "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link on the French dashboard points to the English calculator, switching the user to English.

findings.expected: Use a French image reading "Taux variable : 5,2 %"
findings.description: The French promo image advertises a fixed rate of 4.9% while the English image, the alt text and the page say a variable rate of 5.2%; wrong rate and rate type.
The option to defer the first payment is labelled "Payer maintenant" (Pay now), the opposite of the English "Pay later" and contradicting its help text.
The estimated monthly payment on the French calculator uses the English currency format (leading $ and decimal point).

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Charges" (fees) was translated as "accusation" (criminal charge), which is nonsensical in a banking context.

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve de l'approbation du crédit.
findings.description: The French rate note drops the condition "subject to credit approval".
The dialog's "Close" button was translated as the adjective "Proche" (near) instead of the verb "Fermer".
The French application confirmation page declares html lang="en" although its content is French; other French pages correctly use fr-CA.

findings.observed: Not Found — The requested URL was not found on the server. If you entered the URL manually please check your spelling and try again.
findings.expected: Provide a localized 404 page: "Page introuvable — La page demandée est introuvable. Si vous avez saisi l'adresse manuellement, vérifiez l'orthographe et réessayez."
findings.description: The 404 page under /fr/ is the default server page in English, with no French translation or site navigation.
